item.title: Q1 - Poiseuille's Law and Blood Pressure Regulation
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Cardiovascular Physiology

In mammals, a high blood pressure is needed to achieve a high blood flow (cardiac fluid flow) and to overcome any vascular resistance against the flow of blood. In order to make deductions about blood flow, Poiseuille’s Law is used (Fig.). Poiseuille’s Law: Q = fluid flow, V = volume, t = time, p = pressure, r = vessel radius, η = viscosity (constant for a given temperature and fluid type), L = vessel length, and R = flow resistance.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Assuming similar blood flow in a wide and a narrow artery of the same length, the change in mean blood pressure is greater in the former
B. Increased atherosclerosis leads generally to faster blood flow in the circulation
C. Comparing monozygotic twins, one living at sea level and the other at 3,000 m, the latter will have a higher resistance to blood flow
D. In a specific patient suffering from atherosclerosis, the radius of blood vessels on average had decreased by 1/6, which caused blood pressure to double to maintain the blood flow

item.title: Q10 - The Coagulation Cascade and Vitamin K
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Cardiovascular Physiology

In a classic experiment (1935) by the Danish Nobel laureate H. Dam, chickens that were fed a lipid-depleted diet developed hemorrhage and started bleeding within a couple of weeks, because their uptake of vitamin K was inhibited. The bleeding may be stopped by adding vitamin K to the food (Fig.). The blood coagulation cascade. Several of the pathways involved in coagulation are omitted for reasons of simplification. +, positive regulation; a, active form of compound.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. A mutation called Factor V Leiden causes patients to produce a highly active form of factor V (Va in Fig.), therefore there is an increased risk of embolism
B. Bone-marrow insufficiency leads to increased coagulation
C. A lipid-rich diet may promote coagulation
D. People, suffering from a high risk of embolism, may be treated with heparin (antithrombin activator)

item.title: Q11 - Temperature, Lactic Acid and Salbutamol Effects on Muscle Fatigue
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Muscle Physiology

Muscle fatigue during work results in increasing extracellular concentration of K+. This may be modified by changes in physiological temperature and lactic acid level, and can be treated medically with the drug salbutamol. This was studied experimentally with rat muscles stimulated electrically once every 20 minutes (Fig.). Effect of warm-up at 20°C, 30°C and 35°C before work or addition of lactic acid or a combination of lactic acid and salbutamol at 35°C on the change in muscle force (as percent of force at 4 mM [K+]).

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. During work, contracting muscles lose K+, leading to increased extracellular [K+]
B. Temperature increase, and addition of lactic acid and drug operate mainly additively
C. The study design is incomplete
D. At physiological temperature (here 35°C), lactic acid protects completely against muscle fatigue

item.title: Q12 - Stevioside and Soy Protein Effects on Diabetic Rats
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Endocrine System Physiology

Four groups (A-D), each of 12 diabetic rats, received different diets for four weeks (Table). Researchers wanted to see if a traditional anti- diabetic plant (containing stevioside) had any effect. Four diets (A–D) and measurements of parameters related to diet. BW, body weight. If figures are different, they are here assumed to be significantly so.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. A pure chow diet is not recommended for diabetic rats as it increases cholesterol level and blood pressure
B. SVS and SPI seem to have a synergetic effect
C. Stevioside is harmful to diabetics
D. When fasting, blood glucose results show that there is no statistical difference between the four groups of rats

item.title: Q13 - Countercurrent Heat Exchange in Thermoregulation
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Comparative Thermoregulation

Strategies for regulating body temperature include controlling the movement of blood between the body core and surface and by countercurrent heat exchangers (Fig.). A, Regulation of heat conductance at body surface; B, thermal countercurrent system; C, body temperature in a bird limb. Ta = ambient temperature. Tf = floor temperature.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. In Fig. A, the shunt vessel to the left is exposed to a lower exterior temperature than the one to the right
B. In Fig. B, a countercurrent system often seen in animals from warm habitats is shown
C. The animal in Fig. C lives in a warm habitat
D. In Fig. C, the venous blood at the arrow has a temperature between 14-15°C

item.title: Q14 - C3 and C4 Leaf Anatomy and Climate
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Calvin Cycle, Photorespiration & C4/CAM Biochemistry

Among plant families, grasses and Chenopodiaceae contain many species using the C4 photosynthesis pathway, and many C4 species have evolved independently from C3 ancestors within these families. The figures show cross-sections of C3 and C4 leaf types from different species. Cross section of leaves from: A, C3 species; B, C4 species; C–D, C3 or C4 species. ch = chlorenchyma; at = aqueous tissue; cb = central vascular bundle; hy = hypodermis; pa = palisade cells or mesophyll cells; kr = Kranz cells or bundle-sheath cells.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Evolution of C4 species is favoured in a climate of increasing drought, salinity and heat, but with no change in CO2 level
B. Leaf in Fig. C is from a C3 plant
C. Leaf in Fig. D is from a C3 plant
D. During a period of global CO2 increase, without a concomitant increase in temperature, the global distribution of C4 plants is likely to expand

item.title: Q15 - Chloroplast DNA Haplotypes in a Rare Japanese Orchid
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Genetic Drift, Gene Flow & Mutation

Genetic variation in three chloroplast DNA (cpDNA) regions was studied in populations of a rare orchid Vexillabium yakushimense. Material from nine populations on Honshu and two populations on the Japanese Nansei Islands (Yakushima and Okinawa) were sampled (Fig.). A–B, geographic distribution of 7 cpDNA haplotypes of V. yakushimense. Pies are populations, and each colour indicates a haplotype. The size of each coloured slice shows proportion of each haplotype in the population; C, parsimony network: circles a to g are seven different haplotypes in the 11 populations. Circle size indicates frequency of each haplotype. Linked haplotypes differ by only 1-2 mutations.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. The origin of the orchid in Japan might be mainland Honshu because of the high genetic diversity observed here
B. It is likely that a founder effect can been seen in Okinawa
C. CpDNA is better than nuclear DNA in revealing maternal origins of individuals
D. The study suggests that mountains and river basins are more effective barriers to gene flow than the sea separating islands

item.title: Q16 - Nitrous Oxide Production by Bacteria in Zebra Mussels
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Ecology

Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a greenhouse gas, produced by bacteria through either nitrification or denitrification (Fig. A). Many aquatic invertebrates (e.g. zebra mussel) emit N2O, due to the activity of bacteria in their gut and the biofilm covering their shell (Fig. B, Table). A, pathways for N2O production in bacteria, with key genes amoA (encoding ammonia monooxygenase AMO, nitrification) and nirK (encoding nitrite reductase NIR, denitrification); B, N2O emission from living zebra mussels and shells dissected from living animals, incubated with (+ATU) or without (-ATU) allylthiourea, which is a specific inhibitor of nitrification.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Most N2O in zebra mussel is produced by bacteria inside the animal (e.g. in gut)
B. The N2O production from mussel shells is mostly due to nitrification in their biofilm
C. Nitrification and denitrification are equally important for N2O emission from mussels
D. Increasing nitrate (NO3-) concentrations in lakes (e.g. from agricultural run-off) will increase N2O emissions from freshwater invertebrates

item.title: Q17 - An Adenosine Analogue as a Filovirus Therapeutic
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Nucleotide & Nucleic Acid Chemistry

Filoviruses, e.g. Ebola (EBOV) and Marburg (MAR), cause haemorrhagic fever. Case fatality rates are >90%, and among the highest reported for any human pathogen. Vaccine or therapeutic products are not available. Recently, however, researchers tested an adenosine analogue, BCX, which seemed to improve survival of filovirus-infected humans (Fig.). A, effect of BCX on viral RNA polymerase activity; B, inhibition of EBOV and MAR growth in infected stem cells treated with BCX; C, survival of infected mice after BCX treatments (Tx) administered up to 14 days, beginning either before infection (BI) or post-infection (PI) at varying delays.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. As an adenosine analogue, BCX affects viral gene transcription
B. BCX is applicable exclusively against ebola
C. BCX can successfully (>50% survival) be administered up to 10 days after Ebola infection
D. The half-maximal inhibition of BCX is achieved at a concentration of about 10 μM

item.title: Q18 - The ABC Gene Model of Monocot Flower Development
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Flower Anatomy & Reproductive Structures

Botanists may identify plants to family using diagrams, showing the different floral parts (Fig. A). According to the ABC gene model, development of a flower is based on expression of the A-, class-B- and C-genes. In dicots, sepals develop if gene-A is expressed alone, petals develop if both gene-A and gene-class-B are expressed, stamens develop if both gene-class-B and gene-C are expressed, and an ovary develops if only gene-C is expressed. A, diagram of a monocot flower; B, tulip flower (a monocot), parts of the flower are removed in photo to the right; C, the ABC gene model of monocot flower development (I, ovary; II, stamens; III, petals; IV, sepals; the latter two are similar in most monocots). Gene-class-B consists of 3 genes B1–B3.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Tulips do not have any sepals
B. Gene-C has different expression in monocots and dicots
C. Selective supression of gene C-expression in region II leads to development of unisexual flower
D. Complete development of stamens in the tulip requires the expression of gene-B1+gene-B3+gene-C

item.title: Q19 - Electron Transport Between Oxic and Anoxic Marine Sediment Layers
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Ecology

In the sea, O2 diffuses from the free water down into the top oxic layer in the sediment and here becomes reduced to water. Anoxic layers are beneath this layer, and here bacteria-mediated processes take place. One process is the oxidation of H2S to SO42−, which is tightly coupled to the O2-reduction in the oxic layer above. This coupling between oxic and anoxic processes can only be explained by “electric currents” transporting electrons from H2S oxidation to O2 reduction. In experiments, attempts were made to identify the electron conductor (Fig.). A, physically cut apart by a thin “knife” (before: left diagram, and after: right diagram); B, the two layers were separated by filters with pores of two sizes.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. The pH peak in the oxic layer is due to production of water from oxygen
B. Physically interrupting the sediment by the "knife" did not affect O2 reduction
C. The filters demonstrated that any specific solutes were not transporting the electrons
D. Electrons for the O2-reduction most likely came from donors in the oxic layer

item.title: Q2 - Anion Effects on Hemoglobin Oxygen Affinity
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Respiratory Physiology

O2-binding or -affinity to hemoglobin is affected by specific anions, in particular 2,3 bisphosphoglycerate (BPG) and chloride (Cl−), which are present in red blood cells and bind to the hemoglobin molecule at specific sites (Fig.). Hemoglobin saturation curves for hemoglobin without anions (ctrl) and with BPG, chloride or both, as a function of the partial pressure of oxygen in the blood.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. If peripheral tissue lacks oxygen, red blood cells produce more BPG
B. At high altitudes, mutations leading to changes from polar to non-polar amino acid residues in the BPG binding site of the hemoglobin molecule will be favourable for the affinity of O2 to hemoglobin in the lungs
C. It is likely that chloride and BPG bind at different sites in the hemoglobin molecule
D. BPG decreases the total oxygen saturation capacity of the hemoglobin

item.title: Q20 - Timing Gene Transfer During Bacterial Conjugation
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Linkage, Recombination & Genetic Mapping

In an experiment, two bacterial strains, I and II, were allowed to conjugate. Strain I contained genes allowing it to grow on media lacking arginine and uracil, and with galactose as its sole carbon source, and even in the presence of the antibiotic Kanamycin (+KM). Strain II could not grow on these media. After a certain incubation time, Strain II was grown on selective media until 100 isolated colonies were obtained. The success of conjugation was assessed (Tab.). Table. Success of growth of Strain II in (%) after conjugation.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. The gene marker 'KM resistance' is transferred before the gene required for uracil synthesis
B. The data suggest that a full bacterial genome can be transferred via conjugation in less than 15 minutes
C. The data suggest that a small fraction of recipient colonies can be expected to grow on +KM medium even in the absence of conjugation
D. More than 20% of all colonies incubated for 15 minutes are expected to grow on a medium lacking both arginine and uracil

item.title: Q21 - Cholera Toxin Signaling and a CFTR Inhibitor Treatment
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Cell Signaling & Communication Plasma Membrane Structure & Transport

Cholera is caused by a toxin secreted by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae (Fig. A). One symptom is severe diarrhea, which leads to dehydration and perhaps death. Scientists tested a new CFTR-inhibitor, CFTR-172 (Fig. B) as a potential treatment for cholera. A, action of cholera toxin on an intestinal epithelial cell. GM1 (GM1 ganglioside receptor); Gs (G protein); AC (adenylate cyclase); Gi (G protein); cAMP (cyclic AMP); and CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator Cl- channel); B, dose-dependent reaction of cholera toxin-induced fluid secretion into closed loops of mouse ileum as a function of applied CFTR-172 dose. After the 2010-earthquake in Haiti, a cholera outbreak led to discussions about the origin of the epidemic (Fig. C). Two theories were proposed: Either the infection originated from similar cases in Peru, or UN-soldiers from near Bangladesh carried it to the island, when they came to help after the earthquake. C, five variants of the cholera enterotoxin subunit B open reading frame. “Yellow” loci differ from “red” loci. Labels tell where each variant has caused cholera.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. The water loss of patients with cholera is due to osmosis
B. The cholera toxin binds to transmembrane ion channels thereby starting a cascade reaction
C. Based on Figure B, one might treat cholera-induced diarrhea with CFTR inhibitor, CFTR 172
D. The results in Fig. C support that the cholera outbreak could be caused by infection from the UN soldiers

item.title: Q22 - Adipose Tissue as a Host Response to Skin Infection
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Immune Physiology

Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes skin infection in humans and is a common cause of death. Immediate protection or intervention by local epithelial cells restrict spread of infection. These cells produce antimicrobial peptides (amp), e.g. cathelicidin (Camp). A newly discovered host response to such infections is changes in subcutaneous adipose (fat) tissue (fig A-B). The antibacterial role of this was studied by using BADGE, an ether that inhibits adipogenesis (fig C-E) A, mouse skin infected with SA and compared to control (ctrl); B, change in number and size of adipocytes 3 days after SA infection. C-D, effects of BADGE on wound size and SA CFU (the ether BADGE inhibits adipogenesis, CFU=Colony-Forming Units); E, effects of + and − Camp.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. An SA infection induces the average subcutaneous fat cell to increase in size
B. Number of adipocytes is important against spread of infection
C. Badge destroys the effect of Camp
D. Results in Fig. C-D and in Fig. E support each other well
← Previous: Q21 Next: Q23 →

item.title: Q23 - Rhizobium Nodulation and Gene Structure in Lotus japonicus
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Transcription & RNA Processing

The effect of the nodule bacterium Rhizobium on the growth of the legume Lotus japonicus has often been studied, e.g. in relation to the enzyme/gene system of the interaction (Fig.). A, Rhizobium nodule and the relationship between the number of Rhizobium nodules and the nitrogen (N) content of soil. B, the enzyme CaMK with its mRNA and associated gene. The kinase domain (large dark grey) regulates other enzymes. The black band is the CaM domain, and the four narrow grey bands are EF- hand domains. Boxes in the gene are exons.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Nodulation mainly occurs in nitrogen-poor soil
B. Rhizobium stimulates growth of Lotus by enlarging the surface of its root system; and consequently uptake of NO3- increases
C. Mutation 3G in Fig. B inhibits the transcription of CaMK
D. Each exon encodes a specific protein domain

item.title: Q24 - Competing Hypotheses for Darwin's Finch Diversification
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Coevolution & Species Interactions

The Galápagos Islands are well known for the adaptive radiation of 14 species of finch. The drivers of this radiation are either competition for food in the community of finch species (Hypothesis 1), diversity of available food, i.e. seeds and fruits (Hypothesis 2), or both. Choice of diet is determined by size and structure of the beak. These hypotheses were tested using the six ground finches, which have very different beaks (Fig.). A, relationship between seed/fruit diversity within a habitat and breadth of seed/fruit diet of a finch population in the same habitat. B, relationship between ratio of beak depth of co-occurring pairs of finch species and overlap in consumed food items between a pair of species.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. According to Fig. A, Hypothesis 2 is more likely than Hypothesis 1
B. According to Fig. B, Hypothesis 1 is more likely than Hypothesis 2
C. Different finch species respond to the same extent to an increase in seed and fruit diversity
D. Figures. A–B show that interspecific competition is low when food is more diverse

item.title: Q25 - Coevolutionary Arms Race Between Toxic Newts and Resistant Snakes
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Coevolution & Species Interactions

Rough-skinned Newts (a salamander) produce the toxin TTX, which is lethal to other vertebrates. Individual newts vary in their level of TTX. Garter Snakes eat almost any prey, including newts, and individual snakes vary in their resistance to TTX. The higher the TTX level in a newt population is, the greater the resistance of co-occurring snakes, which, however, still may reject newts, which are too poisonous (Fig.). Relationship between levels of resistance of snakes and toxicity of newts. Each dot represents a site with interacting snake and newt populations. In the white zone, snakes consume newts, but with a cost to their mobility. Dots in grey-coloured zones are toxicity/resistance mismatches.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Coevolution/reciprocal selection between newt and snake mainly takes place in the white zone
B. The figure agrees with the "life-dinner principle", i.e. survival is under stronger selection than demand for food in a prey-predator interaction
C. Per individual, resistance seems to be less costly than toxin production
D. It is likely that the snake populations in the two 'green' and two 'yellow' sites at the extreme right of the figure have won the arms race.

item.title: Q26 - Indirect Effects of Introduced Arctic Foxes on Island Vegetation
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Ecology

The Aleutians Islands west of Alaska are rich in sea birds. The Arctic Fox was not originally present here, but was introduced as a fur game- animal and is now present on many islands. The fox decimates sea bird populations severely. Indirect effects of foxes on island vegetation were compared on islands with and without foxes (Fig.). Mean values for parameters sampled on fox-infested islands (red, left-hand bars) and fox-free islands (blue, right-hand bars). I, view of the plant community on an island; II, logarithm10 of density of breeding sea birds; III, total soil Phosphor; and IV, relative abundance of grasses, shrubs, non-grass herbs, mosses, and others.

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. The study is based on the assumption that sea bird-derived nutrients are distributed all over an island
B. The presence of foxes on an island changes the vegetation from grassland to tundra- shrubland
C. Diversity and number of major plant groups are reduced in islands with fox populations
D. The ecological changes on islands with fox introduction represent exclusively top–down processes

item.title: Q27 - Diet Differences Between Island and Mainland Chough Populations
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Ecology

The bird Red-billed Chough has a wide diet. It lives on the oceanic Spanish island La Palma (IS) and on mainland Spain (MA). The bird’s diet on IS and MA was compared (Fig.). As a food source, invertebrates are rich in protein and lipid, whereas fleshy fruit is rich in carbohydrates. IS-nestlings have more poorly developed feather barbs than MA-nestlings. A, frequency of occurrence in habitat of animal groups; B, chough nestling diet (relative abundance of food item in diet) (from left: Insects, Other arthropods, Other animals, Fleshy fruit, and Seeds).

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Generally, food of animal origin is more scarce on IS than on MA
B. Mainland nestlings have a wider food niche than island populations
C. In general, insects are the favorite food of nestlings
D. Island nestlings are expected to have a faster growth rate and shorter generation time than mainland nestlings

item.title: Q28 - Fruit Availability and Fish Diet Niche in Amazon Floodplains
item.description:
Theoretical A Real exam question - full text reproduced under IBO's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license
Ecology

Within a single year, the Amazon floodplain forests have a high-water (HW) and a low-water (LW) season with a high and low fruit production, respectively. Fruit consumption is widespread among Amazonean fishes, and the relationships between fish diet and fruit production have been explained by three hypotheses H1-H3 (Fig.). Two species of fish (Brycon falcatus and Myloplus asterias) were studied in detail. Three hypotheses (H1-H3) explain how food niche breadth and overlap among fish species (Y) respond to seasonal changes in fruit availability (X).

Figure 1.

Using the information and data, determine which of the statements are true or which are false.

A. Fact: Diet overlap among fish increased from 28% to 95% from low-resource to high-resource season: This relationship is best explained by H1
B. Fact: B. falcatus was, at first, observed not to change its food niche, when food became more plentiful, but then at higher food availability it became increasingly selective: This relationship is best explained by a combination of H1 and H3
C. Fact: Some fish had a constant food niche throughout the year, irrespectively of fruit availability: This is best explained by H1
D. Fact: During HW, M. asterias had a fruit-dominated diet, but switched to leaves instead of fruit in the LW season: This is best explained by H2
